method.method_draft: Use a diagonal decomposition along AC. From the image, note that AB is horizontal, BC is vertical, and the marked square at B indicates triangle ABC is right, with A-B-C consecutive vertices of the convex quadrilateral. From the text, take AB=3 and BC=4, so by the Pythagorean theorem AC=5 and area(ABC)=1/2·3·4=6. Then use the text lengths AD=12 and CD=13; triangle ACD has side lengths 5, 12, 13, so it is a right triangle with legs AC and AD. Its area is 1/2·5·12=30. Add the two triangle areas to get the quadrilateral area 36.

method.method_draft: Use coordinate geometry and the shoelace formula. From the image, place the right angle at B as coordinate axes: let B=(0,0), A=(3,0) along the horizontal segment AB, and C=(0,-4) along the vertical segment BC. From the text, D must satisfy AD=12 and CD=13, so solve (x-3)^2+y^2=144 and x^2+(y+4)^2=169. Subtracting gives 3x+4y=9; choosing the solution on the lower-right side as shown in the image gives D=(63/5,-36/5). Then apply the shoelace formula to the ordered vertices B, A, D, C to obtain area 36.
